_comment: Experiment configuration for harness.py. LSM and workload settings follow
the course P1 (LRU vs HCC) setup. Filter names are <type>-<bits_per_key>
with type bloom, ribbon or cuckoo (e.g. bloom-10, cuckoo-7.5), or none.
For ribbon, bits_per_key is Bloom-EQUIVALENT (same FP rate as Bloom at
that size), so ribbon-N uses ~0.7*N real bits/key; ribbon-14.3 is about
10 real bits/key. Real bits/key per filter is recorded in filters.csv.
Workloads: nonempty (readrandom, all keys exist), empty (readmissing, no
key exists), mixed-F (readrandom with a fraction F of keys absent).
Any other key in fixed/vary is passed to db_bench as -key=value.
threads: "auto" means powers of two up to the number of CPU cores.

E1_bits_per_key.description: FPR, lookup cost and memory vs bits/key for each filter. Cache 256 MB holds all index and filter blocks.

E2_memory_pressure.description: Filters competing with index and data blocks for cache. ribbon-14.3 matches bloom-10 in real memory.

E3_empty_fraction.description: Throughput as the fraction of lookups for absent keys grows.

E4_skew.description: Skewed lookups (read_random_exp_range). Baseline for hotness-aware filters such as ElasticBF.

E5_threads.description: Thread scaling with everything cached (2 GB) after warm-up.
